description: This course covers the fundamentals of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), focusing on user-centered design principles, usability evaluation methods, and interaction techniques. Topics include cognitive models of user behavior; usability testing frameworks such as the System Usability Scale (SUS) and Nielsen's Heuristics; user interface (UI) design for web and mobile applications using Figma and Sketch; interaction paradigms such as direct manipulation and gesture-based interfaces; accessibility standards like WCAG 2.1; and the role of AI in adaptive interfaces. The course also explores prototyping tools like Framer and InVision; user experience (UX) metrics such as task success rates and user satisfaction scores; and the application of human factors in designing for diverse user populations.

clos.text: Define key HCI principles such as user-centered design, usability, and accessibility standards like WCAG 2.1.
Describe the cognitive models of user behavior, including the GOMS model and the cognitive walkthrough technique.
Explain the methodologies for usability testing, including the System Usability Scale (SUS) and Nielsen's Heuristics.
Apply user interface design principles using prototyping tools like Figma and InVision to create wireframes and interactive mockups.
Implement accessibility features in digital interfaces using WCAG 2.1 guidelines and evaluate user experience metrics such as task success rates.
